_README: Rules consumed by .claude/hooks/guardrails.js (PreToolUse on Edit/Write/MultiEdit). The rules below are the UNIVERSAL baseline — safe for any project. Run /bootstrap-claude-pack to append project-specific rules (e.g. vendor-isolation, idempotency keys, no-card-data, module boundaries). Schema is documented at the top of guardrails.js. severity: 'block' (exit 2, Claude must change course) or 'warn' (exit 0 + message). A rule fires only when ALL of its present conditions match.

rules.message: Private key literal in file body. Never commit private keys. Use a secret manager or an env var with a .env.example placeholder.
AWS access key id literal detected. Move it to an env var / secret manager; never commit credentials.
Looks like a hardcoded credential. Read secrets from env vars; keep only placeholders in committed files.
Stripe secret / restricted / webhook-signing key literal. Never commit Stripe secrets — env vars + .env.example placeholders only.
Editing a vendored / generated directory. Changes here are not under source control and will be overwritten. Edit the source, not the build output.
Hand-editing a lockfile. Prefer the package manager (install/add/remove) so the lockfile stays consistent with the manifest.
Editing a CI workflow. Confirm the change is intended — CI config affects every future build and can leak secrets if misconfigured.

A SHORTCUT: marker without an 'upgrade:' trigger is exactly the deferral that rots into permanent. Name the ceiling and the trigger to revisit, e.g. '// SHORTCUT: in-memory list. ceiling: O(n) scan. upgrade: index it when the set grows.' See the keeping-it-lean skill; harvest with /shortcut-ledger.
Exploration budget ε can never be zero or configurable to zero — floor is 0.10, ceiling 0.30 (ADR-0003, CLAUDE.md rule 6). 'A configuration option that can be set to zero will be set to zero.'

No auto-approval exists in this system, ever (REQ-021, won't-change): every APPROVED requires a real human click recorded as human_approved_at. If this is a comment stating the prohibition, fine — otherwise stop.

Only a named human resolution path may clear a veto; model output may never influence veto computation in any direction (REQ-011, rubric-vps-v1 Lane 1). Any code path where model output clears/downgrades a veto is a P1.

organic_publish NEVER implies paid_amplification — no inference path, no config (V4 / ECHO H2). Gate B requires an unexpired paid_amplification grant WITH evidence_uri; a grant without evidence is not a grant.
Organic and boosted performance are recorded as separate series and NEVER summed (REQ-030, measurement-discipline skill).

Calibration and pattern evaluation use TEMPORAL holdouts, never random splits — same-campaign posts share brief/product/audience, so a random split leaks (eval-and-calibration-plan.md). If this split is not on time, stop.

This is a versioned contract of the SUPERSEDED UGC doc set (docs/initial.past/ is frozen history — the active product is Respin under docs/initial/). Editing it is almost certainly a mistake; if the UGC code genuinely needs a contract change, bump the version rather than mutating v1 in place, and keep rubric-vps-v1.md / integration-contract.md consistent.

Tenant A's outcome data never informs Tenant B's scoring — enforced at the repository layer with no widening override and no admin path (tech-spec §Multi-tenancy, compliance-notes). This is not a configuration option.
Anthropic API key literal. Never commit LLM keys — env vars + .env.example placeholders only; no LLM key is ever client-side (Respin tech-spec §6).

NEXT_PUBLIC_* is compiled into the client bundle — a secret under that prefix ships to every browser. Anything named KEY/SECRET/TOKEN belongs server-side (Respin tech-spec §6). Publishable/public keys are the only exception; verify this is one.

packages/ never imports from app/ — the dependency points one way (Respin tech-spec §1: app/ imports packages/; generation logic stays callable from tests without HTTP). Move the shared code into a package instead.

Respin ingests from compliant sources ONLY — YouTube Data API and creator-submitted links; no scraping of closed platforms (REQ-E01, R-4). M4's compliance criterion is a grep-level check that no scraping dependency exists. If this dependency scrapes TikTok/Instagram, stop.

The credit balance is DERIVED (sum of unexpired ledger rows), never stored as a mutable counter (REQ-G04, R-6). A balance column or a balance UPDATE is the violation itself — append a ledger row instead.
Creator and trend baselines use median + MAD, never mean/stddev — engagement distributions are heavy-tailed (tech-spec CreatorBaseline, rubric-vps-v1). Verify this statistic choice is deliberate.
